0.title: Math is Mine
0.objective: I can describe the ways we are all doers of math, and compare my math story with a classmate's.

1.title: Math is Exploring and Thinking
1.objective: I can make sense of a problem, plan a strategy, and use fractions of a whole number to compare quantities.

2.title: Math is In My World
2.objective: I can represent a real-world situation with a tape diagram or table and use decimal operations to solve it.

3.title: Math is Explaining and Sharing
3.objective: I can construct an argument using equations, drawings, or words, and use volume to defend a recommendation.

4.title: Math is Finding Patterns
4.objective: I can find patterns and pattern rules, use them to make generalizations, and check my solutions with a table of values.

5.title: Math is Ours
5.objective: I can describe my problem-solving process, name strategies for getting unstuck, and identify the behaviors that make our class a community of math thinkers.

6.title: Statistical Questions and Data
6.objective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.

7.title: Display Data: Histograms
7.objective: I can make and read a histogram to display data in intervals.

8.title: Mean, Median, and Mode
8.objective: I can find the mean, median, and mode of a data set.

9.title: Display Data: Box Plots
9.objective: I can make and read a box plot to summarize a data set.

10.title: Shape of Data Distributions
10.objective: I can describe the shape of a data distribution as symmetric, skewed, or having clusters and gaps.

11.title: Divide Multi-Digit Numbers
11.objective: I can divide multi-digit whole numbers and explain the meaning of the quotient and remainder.

12.title: Divide Decimals
12.objective: I can divide with decimals by making the divisor a whole number first.

13.title: Mean Absolute Deviation
13.objective: I can find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) to describe how spread out data is.

14.title: Appropriate Measures
14.objective: I can choose the best measure of center for a data set based on its shape.

15.title: Add and Subtract Decimals
15.objective: I can add and subtract decimals by lining up the place values and the decimal points.

16.title: Multiply Decimals
16.objective: I can multiply decimals and place the decimal point correctly in the product.

17.title: Understand Ratios
17.objective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.

18.title: Rates and Unit Rates
18.objective: I can find a unit rate to compare prices and decide the better buy.

19.title: Ratio Tables
19.objective: I can use a ratio table to find equivalent ratios.

20.title: Graph Ratio Tables
20.objective: I can graph the values from a ratio table as points on the coordinate plane.

21.title: Compare Ratios
21.objective: I can compare ratios by finding unit rates or using equivalent ratios.

22.title: Use Ratio Reasoning
22.objective: I can use ratio reasoning to solve problems with proportions and scaling.

23.title: Ratio and Rate Problem Solving
23.objective: I can solve real-world rate problems by finding and using unit rates.

24.title: Solve Problems with Unit Rates
24.objective: I can solve real-world problems by using unit rates to compare options.

25.title: Equivalent Ratios
25.objective: I can find and check equivalent ratios using multiplication and division.

26.title: Convert Measurement Units
26.objective: I can convert measurement units using ratios and conversion factors.

27.title: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
27.objective: I can write and interpret percents greater than 100% and less than 1%.

28.title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents
28.objective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.

29.title: Estimate the Percent of a Number
29.objective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.

30.title: Find the Percent of a Number
30.objective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.

31.title: Use Percent to Solve Problems
31.objective: I can solve problems involving discounts, markups, tax, and tips using percents.

32.title: Area of Parallelograms
32.objective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.

33.title: Area of Triangles
33.objective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.

34.title: Area of Trapezoids
34.objective: I can find the area of a trapezoid using the formula A = ½(b1 + b2) × h.

35.title: Area of Composite Figures
35.objective: I can find the area of a composite figure by adding or subtracting the areas of basic shapes.

36.title: Volume with Whole Number Edges
36.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges using length × width × height.

37.title: Surface Area Using Nets
37.objective: I can find the surface area of a solid by using its net.

38.title: Surface Area of Prisms
38.objective: I can find the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms.

39.title: Surface Area of Pyramids
39.objective: I can find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the base area and the lateral faces.

40.title: Area of Regular Polygons
40.objective: I can find the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into triangles.

41.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
41.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism, including ones with fractional edge lengths, using base area × height.

42.title: Interpret Division of Fractions
42.objective: I can use models to interpret what it means to divide by a fraction.

43.title: Divide Fractions
43.objective: I can divide a fraction by a fraction by multiplying by the reciprocal and simplifying.

44.title: Powers and Exponents
44.objective: I can write and evaluate numbers in exponent form using a base and a power.

45.title: Evaluate Expressions
45.objective: I can evaluate algebraic expressions by substituting values for the variables.

46.title: Write Algebraic Expressions
46.objective: I can write algebraic expressions from words and real-world situations.

47.title: Equivalent Expressions
47.objective: I can show that two expressions are equivalent by simplifying and combining like terms.

48.title: Greatest Common Factor
48.objective: I can find the greatest common factor (GCF) of two numbers by listing or comparing their factors.

49.title: Properties of Operations
49.objective: I can use the commutative, associative, and identity properties to rewrite expressions.

50.title: Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions
50.objective: I can divide a whole number by a fraction by multiplying by the reciprocal.

51.title: Divide Mixed Numbers
51.objective: I can divide mixed numbers by first changing them to improper fractions.

52.title: Fraction Division Problem Solving
52.objective: I can solve real-world problems by writing and solving fraction division equations.

53.title: Least Common Multiple
53.objective: I can find the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers by listing or comparing their multiples.

54.title: Prime Factorization
54.objective: I can write a number as a product of its prime factors using a factor tree.

55.title: The Distributive Property
55.objective: I can use the distributive property to expand and factor expressions.

56.title: Simplify Algebraic Expressions
56.objective: I can simplify algebraic expressions by combining like terms.

57.title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
57.objective: I can place rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, on a number line.

58.title: Integers and Absolute Value
58.objective: I can identify integers and find their absolute value.

59.title: Compare and Order Integers
59.objective: I can compare and order integers using a number line.

60.title: Graph on the Coordinate Plane
60.objective: I can plot and identify points on the coordinate plane using ordered pairs.

61.title: Distance on the Coordinate Plane
61.objective: I can find the distance between two points on the coordinate plane using absolute value.

62.title: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane
62.objective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems.

63.title: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
63.objective: I can plot ordered pairs in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane.

64.title: Reflect Points Across Axes
64.objective: I can reflect points across the x-axis and y-axis on the coordinate plane.

65.title: Write Equations
65.objective: I can write an equation to represent a real-world situation.

66.title: Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations
66.objective: I can solve one-step addition and subtraction equations using inverse operations.

67.title: Solve Multiplication and Division Equations
67.objective: I can solve one-step multiplication and division equations using inverse operations.

68.title: Write Inequalities
68.objective: I can write inequalities to represent real-world situations.

69.title: Graph Inequalities
69.objective: I can graph the solutions of an inequality on a number line.

70.title: Solve and Graph Inequalities
70.objective: I can solve an inequality and graph its solution set on a number line.

71.title: Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving
71.objective: I can model and solve real-world problems using equations and inequalities.

72.title: Explore Relationships Between Two Variables
72.objective: I can recognize when two quantities change together, and identify which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable.

73.title: Analyze Graphs of Relationships Between Two Variables
73.objective: I can use a table and a graph to determine and analyze the relationship between two variable quantities.

74.title: Write Equations to Represent Relationships Between Two Variables
74.objective: I can write an equation from a table or a graph to model the relationship between the dependent and independent variables.

75.title: Apply Two-Variable Relationships to Solve Problems
75.objective: I can write an equation to represent the relationship between two variable quantities and use it to solve a real problem.

76.title: Math is Everywhere
76.objective: I can find applications of math outside of school — in professions like being a chef, in hobbies like gardening, and around my own house.

77.title: Math is Beauty
77.objective: I can use bilateral symmetry to describe structure in nature and in human creations.

78.title: Math is Playful
78.objective: I can use patterns and relationships to make sense of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and think logically about its solutions.

79.title: Math is Ingenuity
79.objective: I can use ratios and models to explain how the Penny Farthing and gear-driven bicycles were ingenious solutions to a real problem.

80.title: Math is Boundless
80.objective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next.

81.title: Math is Mine
81.objective: I can look back at my answers from Lesson 1-1, describe how my math biography has changed this year, and recognize ways we are all doers of math.
